pooling: per-text embedding (batch=1), mean over token axis weighted by attention_mask, then L2-normalised

background.note: recalibrated on the 54-question bank with per-text embedding. Previously the background maximum was a property of batch composition (0.7661 / 0.7727 / 0.8043 / 0.8085 for the same texts at batch sizes 1 / 2 / 54 / 54-per-text). p99/p95/mean/min are now measured on the 54-question bank instead of the 42-question pass.

distribution.note: measured on 1431 pairs of the 54-question bank with per-text embedding. gt_0_80 counts ug_005~ug_006 (0.8085) and fm_002~fm_003 (0.8040). Both are whitelisted as known exceptions.

pooling_note: per-text embedding (batch=1), batch-independent. The pre-fix batch path was not reproducible: the same two question texts scored 0.7661 (batch=1), 0.7727 (batch=2, pipeline with pooling/normalize), 0.8043 (batch=54, batched manual pooling) and 0.8085 (batch=54, per-text). The 0.038 spread exceeded the 0.0043 threshold margin, so every score and duplicate verdict depended on batch composition. Fixed in tools/cosine.cjs embed() by embedding one text per forward pass (nothing to pad, attention_mask is all-ones).

pooling_validation.note: measured on the 54-question bank. batch=2 via --intra-batch on a 2-question file and batch=54 via --self-check now return the identical 0.7661 for ug_003~ug_004 (those two texts are byte-identical in the bank and in that file). The pipeline figure is a separate 2-text call with { pooling: 'mean', normalize: true }; the plain pipeline() call with no options returns a 3D token matrix, which cannot be cosined directly.
pooling_validation.max_pair_shift: under the old batched embedding the 54-question maximum was ug_003~ug_004 (0.8043); with per-text embedding it is ug_005~ug_006 (0.8085) and ug_003~ug_004 falls to 0.7661

threshold_margin.verdict: the threshold sits 0.0085 BELOW the measured background maximum, so exactly two pairs exceed it under per-text embedding: ug_005~ug_006 (0.8085) and fm_002~fm_003 (0.8040). ug_005 and ug_006 are two differently-worded questions about the same operation (adding a user to a supplementary group); fm_002~fm_003 are a file-management pair. Both pairs were judged acceptable in human review, so this is an artifact of the compressed Russian-text range in an English model, not an unnoticed duplicate. Both stay in known_exceptions; the threshold is unchanged at 0.80 by explicit decision.

threshold_warning: 0.80 < background_max. New pairs > 0.80 will be auto-rejected. L5c (intra-batch manual review) required before accepting new batches.
calibration_note: Recalibrated after the batch-independence fix (per-text embedding). ug_003~ug_004 dropped out of the whitelist (0.7661); fm_002~fm_003 (0.8040) and ug_005~ug_006 (0.8085) stay whitelisted. Threshold unchanged at 0.80 by explicit decision.
justification: The pre-fix embed() scored a padded batch, so a text's vector depended on the longest text beside it and the measured maximum was a property of batch composition, not of the corpus. per-text embedding (batch=1) removes padding entirely and is reproducible: ug_003~ug_004 returns 0.7661 in a 2-question file, inside the 12-question pending batch and inside the 54-question bank. On the recalibrated 54-question bank the maximum is ug_005~ug_006 = 0.8085 with 2 pairs above 0.80, 2 above 0.78, 5 above 0.75 and 21 above 0.70. Under the old batched embedding the same bank reported 1 pair above 0.80 (ug_003~ug_004 = 0.8043).
note: The cosine threshold remains 0.80 by explicit decision and was not changed. Because background_max 0.8085 now exceeds it, any future batch containing a pair at that similarity will be auto-rejected unless it is listed in known_exceptions.
caveat: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 is an English model; cosine scores on Russian text are compressed (paraphrase 0.49 vs unrelated 0.42 in a short probe), so the dynamic range is much narrower than for English. This is why topically-related but distinct questions can reach 0.80.

recalibration_history.note: current; batch-independent, verified identical at batch=1/2/54
